group_scores.rationale: In-window evidence is mostly T3 (Oilprice.com, The National) and points to a supply-led downturn: Brent about $91-92 against more than $110-118 in October, OPEC+ output rising, Saudi discounts, IEA surplus reported second-hand. Against that, T2 Al Jazeera reports an ongoing Hormuz escalation: the US strike on Qeshm, Iranian attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain, a MARAD warning on war-risk premia, and Houthi threats to Saudi ports. These cut both ways, and there is no T1/T2 source on the oversupply side. Score 0.
group_scores.falsifier: T1/T2 confirmation of the surplus (IEA OMR direct, OPEC MOMR, Reuters survey) or an OPEC+ hike on about 30 Nov would argue for -1. An actual Hormuz closure or confirmed damage to Saudi infrastructure would argue for +1.

group_scores.rationale: T1 MoF shows routine Saudi sukuk issuance (SAR 2.257bn) in the window. The FY2027 pre-budget deficit of about SAR 190bn is background from Oct. T2 Al Jazeera reports Houthi damage to the PIF tower in Riyadh and Iranian attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain, which is risk premium. Flows are recovering and the UAE gets favourable treatment under the BIS rule. No MSCI, CBUAE or market-performance data was found. The evidence is mixed, so the default is 0.
group_scores.falsifier: MSCI deletions or weight cuts, a CBUAE/SAMA liquidity notice, a confirmed strike on Saudi oil infrastructure, or a much larger Saudi 2027 deficit would argue for -1. A US-Iran reopening deal or MSCI inclusions would argue for +1.

group_scores.rationale: WGC (T2) places the risk-off in the AI-equity rout and hawkish Fed minutes, not geopolitics. Taiwan MND (T1) shows routine activity. Daily GPR (T1) is near its Oct mean and below the 2026 YTD mean. There is no Russia-Ukraine ceasefire, and talks show no breakthrough (T3). Geopolitics gives no in-window reason to move.
group_scores.falsifier: A Russia-Ukraine ceasefire or a sharp escalation, a PLA exercise or blockade, or a collapse of the US-China truce in the window.

group_scores.rationale: PBoC bought 26t in Oct, its most since Oct 2023 (WGC T2, verified), so official-sector demand is firm. Against that, WGC reports a sell-off over 16-20 Nov on Fed hike expectations, a stronger USD and easing oil, with no geopolitical premium cited. The forces offset, so the score is 0. The verifier capped confidence at low.
group_scores.falsifier: A geopolitical flare-up restoring the premium, or the Fed stepping back from a Dec hike, would argue for +1. A confirmed Dec hike with dollar strength and slowing CB buying would argue for -1.
